plans.rationale: This is the first round of investigation for INC-04. We need to establish the exact symptom onset and check error rates and connection pool metrics for payments-api and ledger-service, as well as investigate all recent dependency changes, deploys, and infrastructure events across the system.

tasks.goal: Check error rates, connection pool exhaustion metrics, and logs for payments-api and ledger-service from 12:00 to 13:50 to determine exact symptom onset and nature of the database connection errors.
Review all recent config changes, deploys, feature flags, and infrastructure changes over the last 7 days for payments-api, ledger-service, ledger-db, and their surrounding dependency map.
Check error rates, connection pool exhaustion metrics, and logs for payments-api and ledger-service from 12:00 to 13:50 to determine exact symptom onset and nature of the database connection errors.
Review all recent config changes, deploys, feature flags, and infrastructure changes over the last 7 days for payments-api, ledger-service, ledger-db, and their surrounding dependency map.
Build and rank competing root-cause hypotheses

r1-dependency-2.summary: Reviewed dependencies and recent changes for payments-api, ledger-service, and ledger-db. Found that ledger-service had a dependency bump deploy on 2026-10-03 and a critical configuration change on 2026-10-06 at 13:12 reducing db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5, which immediately precedes the reported incident at 13:15.

findings.statement: payments-api depends synchronously on ledger-service, upi-gateway, fraud-service, and redis-cache, and asynchronously on event-bus.
ledger-service underwent a dependency bump deploy (v2.12.7) on 2026-10-03 at 16:53.
ledger-service underwent a config change on 2026-10-06 at 13:12 normalizing db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5.
No deploys or configuration changes were found for payments-api or ledger-db over the 7-day lookback window.

open_questions: What were the exact metrics and error rates for ledger-service and ledger-db immediately following the 13:12 config change?

r1-observability-1.summary: Payments-api and ledger-service experienced a sudden surge in errors and latency starting precisely at 2026-10-06T13:15:00+00:00 due to database connection pool exhaustion in ledger-service.

findings.statement: payments-api error rate spiked up starting at 2026-10-06T13:15:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 8.26% at 13:47.
ledger-service error rate spiked starting at 2026-10-06T13:15:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 10.25% at 13:45.
ledger-service p99 latency anomaly began at 2026-10-06T13:14:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 7278.17ms.
ledger-service logs show HikariPool connection timeouts indicating pool exhaustion (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting) starting at 2026-10-06T13:15:05+00:00.
payments-api logs show errors calling ledger-service due to inability to acquire connections starting at 2026-10-06T13:15:02+00:00.
ledger-db active connections and cpu percentage dropped significantly starting at 2026-10-06T13:13:00+00:00.

open_questions: What caused ledger-db or the network path between ledger-service and ledger-db to drop active connections suddenly at 13:13?

hypotheses.title: Configuration Change Reducing Database Connection Pool Size Exhausts Ledger Service Connections
hypotheses.mechanism: A configuration change normalized the maximum database connection pool size from 50 to 5, which immediately restricted available connections under normal traffic load, causing connection timeouts and downstream errors in payments-api.

supporting.note: Config change on ledger-service at 13:12 reduced db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5, immediately preceding the onset.
Ledger-service latency anomaly began at 13:14, right after the config change.
Ledger-service error rate spiked starting at 13:15.
Payments-api error rate spiked starting at 13:15 as calls to ledger-service failed.
Ledger-service logs show HikariPool connection timeouts indicating pool exhaustion (total=5, active=5) starting at 13:15.
Payments-api logs show errors calling ledger-service due to inability to acquire connections starting at 13:15.

assumptions: The configuration change applied successfully across all running instances of ledger-service instantly.

hypotheses.title: Upstream Traffic Surge Overwhelming Ledger Service
hypotheses.mechanism: An unexpected increase in request concurrency caused ledger-service connections to exhaust.

supporting.note: Payments-api error rates spiked during the incident.

contradicting.note: Payments-api RPS shows no abnormal surge or traffic spike during the window.
The config change at 13:12 provides a direct and sufficient explanation for connection exhaustion without needing a traffic spike.

assumptions: Internal query complexity increased significantly at 13:15.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: The onset is firmly established at 2026-10-06T13:14:00+00:00 with the latency anomaly on ledger-service. Configuration change chg-8919 occurred at 13:12, reducing the connection pool size from 50 to 5, which directly triggered pool exhaustion and errors across ledger-service and payments-api at 13:15. H1 is exceptionally well-supported by both change logs and runtime metrics.

adjustments.reason: Directly supported by configuration change chg-8919 reducing max connection pool size at 13:12, precisely preceding the onset of ledger-service latency at 13:14 and connection pool exhaustion errors at 13:15.
